decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: paste URL + 'Save link', prototype 'filled in the title "JavaScript | MDN" and a little description on its own, plus it shows where it came from'. Client r4: 'That's just what I hoped for.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-URL and auto-collect of title/description/source conform to REF-BM-01/02. Favicon/preview-image sub-parts never demonstrated but not explicitly excluded; insufficient evidence to establish a divergence, so treated as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'I assumed new links begin as To read'. Client r4: 'New links starting as To read makes sense to me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Default unread ('To read') state conforms to REF-BM-17 read-later concept.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: whole card selectable, opens original page. Client r5: 'I clicked the JavaScript | MDN card and it opened the actual MDN page.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting a list item navigates to the original url — conforms to REF-BM-08. Whole-card vs link target is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker asked only about return-to-page behaviour after re-saving the same MDN url; the second save's outcome was unclear ('it just showed the one card again'). Client r5: 'if I try to save a link I've already got, it shouldn't quietly make a second copy... recognize "you already saved this one" and just take me to the existing one... Can you show me what happens?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The asked-about scope (navigation) omitted duplicate handling; presented behaviour did not surface the REF-BM-06 guide-to-existing rule. Client surfaced the missing reference requirement and requested alignment. Fulfilled at round 6 (conforming re-presentation, not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'It should tell you the link is already saved, keep only one copy... I've treated two exactly matching web addresses as the same link.' Client r6: 'Yes, that's the behavior I wanted... kept just the one copy.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Revised conforming presentation of REF-BM-06 following the round-5 capture; recorded as conforming, not counted as a new opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: three UI versions for adding the label 'reference'; label appears as a chip beneath details. Client r7 selects Version 1 and confirms chip presentation.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning a tag conforms to REF-BM-09; the three add-method variants are functionally equivalent UI (all fulfil REF-BM-09) — an orthogonal preference, not a divergence/select.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 label-add flow presented no autocomplete. Client r7: 'as I start typing, I'd like it to suggest labels I've already used, so I don't accidentally make "reference" and "References" and "ref" as three separate ones... Can you keep that in mind for the label typing?'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented tag-entry omitted REF-BM-10 autocomplete; client surfaced the missing reference requirement and requested it. Fulfilled at round 8 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker: suggestions from labels used anywhere, prefix match, case-insensitive. Client r8: 'I typed "ref" and it immediately offered "reference"... this makes label reuse feel consistent.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming presentation of REF-BM-10 autocomplete following the round-7 capture; case-insensitive matching also conforms (REF-BM-13). Not counted as a new opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: click the 'javascript' chip / label row to filter. Client r9: 'the collection narrowed down to just the two links carrying that label.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-filter conforms to REF-BM-11; two activation points are an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker: search matches titles, descriptions, source names, case-insensitive, with label filter still active. Client r10: 'Searching across the title, the description, and the source name all at once is right... Not caring about capital letters.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search over title/description and case-insensitivity conform to REF-BM-12/13; label+search combine (REF-BM-11). Note and url coverage handled as separate decisions below.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 client: 'eventually I'll be jotting my own little notes on some bookmarks, and when that exists I'd want the search to look inside those notes too... just so search is designed with that in mind.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented search omitted the note field required by REF-BM-12; client surfaced the missing sub-requirement and requested it. Fulfilled at round 15 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Maker repeatedly framed search fields as 'titles, descriptions, and source names' (r10) and the final summary as 'my titles, descriptions, notes and sources' (r18). REF-BM-12 specifies full-text over the url. Client adopted 'sources' language throughout and never expressed the url-vs-source-name difference.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Searching the display source (domain) rather than the full url is a stated scope decision that diverges from REF-BM-12's url coverage (path/query tokens not indexed). The client never surfaced or expressed this difference; passed under approval.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker: three UI versions to flip To read <-> Done. Client r11 selects Version 1, valuing the two-way toggle.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Marking read/unread both ways conforms to REF-BM-17/19; the three status-control UIs are functionally equivalent — orthogonal preference, not a select over differing fulfilment.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: To read / Done separated views with counts, immediate move. Client r12 picks Version 1 (top tabs); 'it vanished from To read... clicked over to the Done tab and there it was.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Separate unread/done views conform to REF-BM-18; tabs-vs-columns are equivalent UI variants.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker presented the edit flow (title, note, label, side panel, note visible). Client r13: 'I couldn't change the description... I also couldn't fix the web address itself... Can you add those two into this same edit panel?'
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review. The presented 'edit a bookmark' panel omitted description and url editing required by REF-BM-04; client caught the partial divergence and requested the missing fields. Title/note/tag editing and note display (REF-BM-04/23) conformed. Fulfilled at round 14 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 14 maker: change description and remove '?utm_source=newsletter' from address, save. Client r14: 'both fields are there now and they work... the new description and the cleaned-up address.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming re-presentation completing REF-BM-04 editing after the round-13 capture. Showing short source vs full url on cards is an orthogonal display preference (REF-BM-07 does not require url on cards).

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker: search 'closures' matches only via the note; note text searchable, case-insensitive, combinable with labels. Client r15: 'searching my own notes is in.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming presentation of the note-search sub-requirement of REF-BM-12 captured at round 10. Not counted as a new opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker asked 'does this complete the search behavior?' Client r15: 'Searching by a label right in the search box... type something like #reference in the search and have it treat that as "only things with the reference label".'
decisions.note: Specification/prototype review. In response to a completeness claim, client surfaced the missing REF-BM-14 #tag search. Fulfilled at round 16 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 15 client: 'Combining conditions... something like "anything about rome that's either an article or a book" — being able to say "this AND (that OR the other)", and to say "not this". Right now search seems to look for the whole thing I typed as one lump.'
decisions.note: Specification/prototype review. Client surfaced the missing REF-BM-15 AND/OR/NOT + parentheses behaviour against a completeness claim. Fulfilled at round 17 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 15 client: 'Exact phrases. If I put something in quotes, I'd want it matched exactly as written, rather than each word on its own.' Reiterated r17.
decisions.note: Specification/prototype review. Client surfaced the missing REF-BM-16 quoted-phrase exact match against a completeness claim. Fulfilled at round 18 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 16 (#reference inline), round 17 ('rome AND (#article OR #book) AND NOT ancient'), round 18 ('"a weekend"'). Client approves each: r18 'search now feels complete to me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming presentations of REF-BM-14/15/16 following the round-15 captures; recorded as conforming, not counted as new opportunities.

decisions.evidence: Round 26 maker asked whether to actively monitor pages or just preserve saved info. Client r26: 'when I first save a link, I'd love it to keep a copy of the page as it was at that moment, so if the page later changes or disappears I can still see what I saved.'
decisions.note: Specification review. Client proactively surfaced the REF-BM-24 local snapshot requirement (distinct from the monitoring question asked). Fulfilled at round 27 (not double-counted).

decisions.evidence: Round 27 maker: auto-capture readable copy on save, open inside Link Home; three surfacing UIs. Client r27 picks Version 3; 'Automatically capturing a readable copy when I save is exactly what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming presentation of REF-BM-24 snapshot following the round-26 capture. The REF-BM-24 PDF sub-rule was never presented or raised — no presented decision to classify (excluded, insufficient evidence).

decisions.evidence: Round 32 maker summary of '26 feature and edge-case flows' lists saving, duplicates, labels, search, To read/Done, editing, live/preserved pages, recovery — no delete. Client r32 approves ('go ahead and start building it'); r33 acceptance describes no delete capability. Deleting a bookmark never raised anywhere.
decisions.note: Specification gate. The approved scope omits REF-BM-05 (delete). Client's generic caveat ('a few ordinary needs we haven't talked about yet') does not identify this specific requirement, so it is bare acknowledgment, not accepted_divergence. Passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 32 scope summary and round 33 acceptance contain no multi-select or bulk actions; never presented or raised across rounds 1-33.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-20/21 (select multiple bookmarks; apply bulk action to the whole filtered collection). Client never surfaced these; generic caveat does not identify them. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: No sort/ordering flow anywhere; round 32 summary and round 33 acceptance make no mention of sorting by a sort key.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-22 (sort by date added, title, etc.). Client never surfaced it. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Snapshot discussion (rounds 26-28) covered only a local page copy; Internet Archive snapshot never mentioned in round 32 summary or elsewhere.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-25 (Internet Archive snapshot). Client never surfaced it. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 32 summary lists To read/Done management but no archive; archiving (hide-but-keep), archive-vs-delete distinction, and an archived-only list never appear in any round. (Round 26 concerned live-page monitoring, a different, non-reference concern.)
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits the archive feature set (REF-BM-26/27/28). Client never surfaced it; generic caveat does not identify it. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Client engaged deeply with search+label filtering (rounds 9-18) but the ability to save a search-term/tag combination as a reusable bundle is never presented or raised; absent from round 32 summary.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-29 (saved bundles/filters). Despite extensive filtering discussion, client never surfaced persisting a filter. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Client's opening problem was existing scattered browser bookmarks (r1), yet Netscape-HTML import is never presented or raised; absent from round 32 summary and round 33 acceptance.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-30 (import). Client never surfaced migrating existing bookmarks. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Export in Netscape HTML never presented or raised anywhere; absent from round 32 summary.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-31 (export). Client never surfaced it. Unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Display settings (default sort, displayed items, font size) never presented or raised; round 29's Show more/less was an in-card UI treatment, not a persisted personal setting. Absent from round 32 summary.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Approved scope omits REF-BM-32 (display-related personal settings). Client never surfaced it. Unexpressed.
